留出评论标题: Delicious and convenient, but with caveats
留出评论文本:
Make no mistake - this rice is convenient and packed with flavor. If you have no dietary restrictions and are physically active then you will probably love this for a number of reasons.

Foremost is convenience. In 90 short seconds you can have perfectly prepared grains that are plump and steamed to perfection. That alone makes this wonderful because properly steaming wild rice requires a pressure cooker and about forty minutes. Adding in the faster cooking long grain rice would entail steaming them separately and mixing them.

Second is the flavor. Undeniably delicious and can stand by itself as a side dish or combined with meat, fish or vegetables to be en entree.

Where the problems surface is if you are on a restricted diet, especially for sodium. This package contains a stratospheric sodium level and more than nominal fat content. Sodium is over the top at 690mg per serving. Fat is 2.5 grams a serving and account for 25 of the 210 calories. Those undo the health benefits of wild and long grain rice as a part of a balanced diet for those of us who have to count sodium and fat intake. Moreover, while the fat in this product is not particularly bad for folks who are young and active, the sodium is at levels that I consider to be too high for any diet.

I get around the sodium and fat problems by 'cutting' this with steamed jasmine or basmati rice I prepare then mixing this into the plain steamed rice. It works out well when I am cooking for company. A final note; follow the directions and this will cook perfectly. Especially Step 2 listed on the back of the package that requires you to tear back two inches at the notch on the top left side of the package. Failure to do that (or cooking longer than 90 seconds in a microwave) can get messy.

留出评论标题: Very good popcorn at a value price!
留出评论文本:
As I'm married to a man whose eaten a huge bowl of popcorn almost every night for 44 yrs. I've become pretty much an expert on what's good & what ain't. This Amish® brand (which, since I live near a large Amish community I doubt is nothing more than a company name, not grown by Amish) is one of the best we've tried.

It's extremely fresh so it pops cleanly with very few unpopped kernels. When I got the popcorn I was worried that the end result wouldn't be very large when popped as the kernels were not that big. The first time I made it the pops were not huge, but they were much bigger than expected. They tasted quite good, too.

I make our popcorn two ways: 1) I pop it in a dedicated stainless steel covered pan in oil, with butter & theater salt and 2) a microwave silicone popper ($15.99 on Amazon) using no oil, spritz the hot popcorn with I Can't Believe It's Not Butter® spray, then dust mine with Kernel Seasons ® (I have the set of 7 & & mix n match different ones i.e Jalapeno with Nacho or White Cheddar with Kettle Corn [sounds weird but tastes great] etc.
This makes for a very low-cal high-fiber snack. These are available on Amazon under 'popcorn seasonings' Oh, and those seasonings are good for lots more than popcorn: I've used them on a number of other things, like in sauces & salad dressings to name a few. )

The big bag of popcorn seeds received will only last us a short time compared to most other folks, so if you own a vacuum sealer (can't live without mine as sealing boxed stuff up as it not only saves room it keeps bugs from getting in my kitchen as well) this is a good way to keep some of most of the popcorn seeds fresh longer. Don't have one? I tried the Seal-a-Meal® but it wore out way too fast & they don't sell replacement heating wires. So, I bought a Koios®. It's available on Amazon for $80 bucks which is a lot less than the other but comes with a spare heating wire included. Plus the Koios has more functions than the higher priced 'name' models.

Since I liked this brand of popcorn so much...and,more importantly, so did hubby...I'll definitely be buying Amish ® brand again. Good taste at a value price.
